$comment: What in this repository is the standard, what is this product, and what is neither. Checked by tools/check_boundary.py: a directory that holds source and is not classified here fails CI, so the question gets answered when the code is written and the answer is cheap.

src/iaes.why: Expresses an IAES event and nothing else: the published vocabulary, asset identity, the envelope, the canonical form and the specification's content hash. A competitor implementing IAES needs to ask us nothing to use it.

src.why: Deadbands, thresholds, when a value deserves a severity, and how this runtime talks to a device. All of it is judgment or transport, and neither is part of the standard.

profiles.why: An equipment catalog. GOVERNANCE.md section 1.2 excludes these from IAES by name, thresholds included. Seven profiles, 174 registers, 29 thresholds.

examples.why: Shows this runtime being configured, not the standard being implemented.

tools.why: Repository plumbing: it neither implements the standard nor ships in the product.

test.why: Conformance and unit tests. They exercise both sides without belonging to either.

the_rule: Nothing under a directory classed 'standard' may include a file from outside it. That is the whole boundary in one sentence, and it is the one that broke: until 2026-09-06 IaesEvent.h included IaesDetector.h, so producing a standard event required running this product's judgment first.
